Tencent Holdings Limited, an investment holding company, provides value-added services, marketing services, fintech, and business services in Mainland China and internationally. The company's consumers business includes communications and social services, such as instant messaging and social networks; digital content, including online games, videos, live streaming, news, music, and literature; fintech services, which include mobile payment, wealth management, consumer loans, and securities trading; and various tools comprising network security management, browsing, navigation, application management, email, etc. Its enterprise business comprises marketing solutions, which offer digital tools, including user insight, creative management, placement strategy, and digital assets management; and cloud services, such as cloud computing, big data analytics, artificial intelligence, Internet of Things, and security and other technologies for financial services, education, healthcare, retail, industry, transport, energy, and radio and television industries. The company also invests in, produces, and distributes films and television programs; offers copyrights licensing and merchandise sales and other services; provides internet advertisement services; and offers software development, and information technology and system integration services, as well as develops and operates mobile games. # Hong Kong Tech Stocks Surge Nearly 6% in a Single Day, Meituan Leads Gains as Southbound Funds Reverse Course

- Published: 2026-11-05T04:06:02.000Z
- Updated: 2026-11-05T12:11:44.000Z
- Author: BigGo Editorial Team
- Keywords: Hang Seng Tech Index, Hang Seng Index, Meituan-W, Tencent Holdings, Alibaba-W, NetEase, Xiaomi Group-W, Southbound Funds, U.S. Midterm Elections, Tencent Hunyuan Hy4, CICC, CITIC Securities

## Summary

On November 5, all three major Hong Kong stock indices rallied sharply, with the Hang Seng Tech Index closing up 5.55% — its largest single-day gain of the year — while the Hang Seng Index rose 3.67% to reclaim the 24,000-point level. Tech and internet stocks surged collectively: NetEase gained over 9%, Xiaomi and Alibaba rose more than 8%, Tencent climbed over 7%, and Meituan briefly rose nearly 10% intraday. Following the conclusion of the U.S. midterm elections, global capital rotated from AI hardware into undervalued Chinese internet assets, compounded by short covering and a swing in Southbound Funds from net outflow to net inflow, jointly driving this rebound. AI hardware, optical communications, and PCB sectors bucked the trend and corrected. Institutions believe the short-term rebound stems from valuation and sentiment repair, while a medium-term trend reversal still depends on corporate earnings and improvement in domestic demand.

## Content

On November 5, the Hong Kong stock market staged a long-awaited strong rally. The Hang Seng Tech Index approached a 6% gain intraday before closing up 5.55% at 4,154.29 points, marking its largest single-day gain of the year. The Hang Seng Index rose 3.67% in tandem to close at 24,796.98 points, reclaiming the 24,000-point threshold; the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index gained 3.87% to 8,369.08 points.

Tech and internet stocks were the undisputed driving force behind the session. Meituan-W (03690.HK) rose as much as 9.6% intraday before closing up 6.78%; NetEase (09999.HK) gained 9.07%, Xiaomi Group-W (01810.HK) rose 8.83%, Alibaba-W (09988.HK) climbed 8.45%, Tencent Holdings (00700.HK) advanced 7.17%, JD.com-SW (09618.HK) rose 6.95%, and Baidu-W (09888.HK) gained 5.36%. Consumer, automotive, real estate, and pharmaceutical/biotech sectors also ranked among the top gainers, while oil and petrochemicals, coal, and AI hardware-related names bucked the trend and declined.

Triple Rotation Compounded by Short Covering

In terms of catalysts, a collective rally in U.S.-listed Chinese stocks overnight provided external groundwork for Hong Kong equities. The Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index closed up 3.49% at 5,722.71 points, with popular Chinese ADRs broadly higher. The more critical shift came from a change in global capital style — following the conclusion of the U.S. midterm elections,阶段性 political uncertainty was largely eliminated, and some capital began withdrawing from richly valued AI hardware and semiconductor names, rotating into lower-valuation Chinese internet platforms more closely tied to consumer demand.

Bloomberg Intelligence strategist Marvin Chen characterized the phenomenon as a triple rotation: a regional rotation from markets such as South Korea into China, a value rotation from high-valuation assets into low-valuation assets, and a trading rotation from AI hardware and pure-play AI names into other tech assets.

Hong Kong internet assets had previously undergone a deep correction. The Hang Seng Tech Index's forward price-to-earnings ratio had fallen to about 13x last month, the lowest level since 2024. Calculations by China Securities (CSC) showed that as of October 25, the index's forward P/E stood at approximately 14.5x, in the 7th percentile of its historical range, down roughly 75% from its peak of 50-60x in early 2021. Gavekal Capital portfolio manager Leonid Mironov said some Hong Kong-listed companies have become very cheap and investors are attempting to bottom-fish.

Extreme pessimism also provided fuel for the rebound. CICC statistics showed that as of October 30, the Hang Seng Tech Index's sentiment indicator had fallen to negative 0.95, in the 2nd percentile since 2021, breaching the negative 0.82 dynamic panic trigger line; only 13.33% of constituent stocks stood above their 50-day moving averages. Lotus Asset Management Chief Investment Officer Hao Hong argued that the U.S. midterm elections constituted a mean-reversion event for both U.S. politics and the Hong Kong stock market — Hong Kong equities had been oversold, triggering one of the larger short squeezes in recent years. The options market also showed signs of improving sentiment, with the Hang Seng Tech Index's three-month implied volatility falling to its lowest level since July, and options trading volume tracking the Tracker Fund of Hong Kong rising to a one-year high.

Funding Flows Show Early Turning Point; Earnings Delivery Remains Key

Fund flows showed substantive changes. In October, Southbound Funds recorded cumulative net selling of approximately HK$27.951 billion (approximately $3.6 billion), including a net outflow of HK$ 11.036 billion (approximately $1.4 billion) in the week of October 26-30, with selling pressure highly concentrated during the accelerated decline in late October. But by midday on November 3, intraday net inflows of Southbound Funds into Hong Kong stocks had exceeded HK$ 12 billion (approximately $1.5 billion), breaking a streak of 14 consecutive trading days of sustained net outflows.

Individual stocks also showed signs of increased capital commitment. Hong Kong Stock Exchange disclosure-of-interests data showed that on October 29, 2026, JPMorgan increased its long position in Meituan-W by 49.7671 million shares at an average price of HK$65.9604 (approximately $8.4) per share, involving approximately HK$ 3.283 billion (approximately $418.5 million).

Tencent Holdings' advance was further supported by technological progress. The company's Hunyuan team officially released its next-generation large language model "Hunyuan Hy4," with a parameter scale of 770B (770 billion), achieving significant breakthroughs in instruction following, deep long-text comprehension, and long-horizon agent capabilities. Tencent said it will open-source the model weights in the near future and previewed that the next-generation Hy5 model will further expand its parameter scale. CICC maintained its "Outperform" rating on Tencent Holdings with a target price of HK$666 (approximately $85), corresponding to 2026 and 2027 Non-IFRS P/E ratios of 20x and 19x, respectively.

The pharmaceutical sector was also active. Sino Biopharmaceutical (01177.HK) announced after market close on November 4 a major out-licensing deal with multinational pharmaceutical company Boehringer Ingelheim for next-generation oncology therapies, covering six innovative drug preclinical programs; the stock closed up 9.22% that day. BeiGene (06160.HK) rose 7.34%, Akeso (09926.HK) gained 6.48%, and Innovent Biologics (01801.HK) added 4.12%.

Gold stocks followed international gold prices higher in a rebound, with spot gold breaking through both the $4,000/oz and $4,100/oz thresholds, rebounding about 7% from recent lows. Laopu Gold (06181.HK) rose 8.32%, Zhaojin Mining (01818.HK) gained 5.85%, and Zijin Gold International (02259.HK) added 4.87%, all hitting two-week highs.

AI Hardware Under Pressure; Institutions Flag Structural Opportunities

In contrast to the fervor in tech and internet stocks, the AI hardware sector corrected collectively that day. The market worried that the U.S. Democratic Party may subsequently introduce stricter regulatory requirements targeting the high power consumption and infrastructure access of AI data centers, triggering profit-taking in U.S. semiconductor and data center names. South Korea's stock market opened sharply lower and trended down that day, with the KOSPI closing down more than 5%, and both Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plunging more than 7%, further suppressing risk appetite for AI hardware across Asia.

In the Hong Kong market, Montage Technology (06809.HK) fell 6.63% and GigaDevice (03986.HK) dropped 5.06%; in the optical communications sector, Yangtze Optical Fibre and Cable (06869.HK) fell 12.48% and Nanzhen Technology (09856.HK) dropped 7.89%; among PCB-related names, Kingboard Laminates (01888.HK) fell 12.43% and Guanghe Technology (01989.HK) dropped 8.28%.

For the outlook, institutional views show a consensus amid clear divergence. CICC believes that Hong Kong stocks' current low valuations and oversold sentiment have created favorable odds for a short-term rebound, but achieving a genuine trend reversal still hinges on whether the household credit cycle can materially improve, which requires further fiscal policy efforts tilted more toward the household sector. CITIC Securities expects Hang Seng Index and Hang Seng Composite Index earnings to grow 7.4% and 9.9% respectively in 2027, with the Hang Seng Tech Index's earnings growth potentially reaching 24.8%, and consumption and technology expected to succeed cyclicals as the main incremental sources of earnings growth; it also expects the Federal Reserve may restart rate cuts in the second half of 2027, easing discount-rate pressure.

HuaTai Securities Chief Macro Economist Yi Huan believes the peak of macro liquidity pressure on Hong Kong stocks may have passed, but constraints will be difficult to fully remove; opportunities in Hong Kong stocks will come more from structural earnings improvement and global capital rebalancing, with a sentiment-repair rebound likely in the short term, while the medium-term deciding factor remains progress in domestic demand improvement.

# South Korea's Samsung Electronics Falls Below 200,000 Won; Brokerages Say "Entering Historically Undervalued Zone… Consider Buying in Tranches"

- Published: 2026-11-08T08:25:32.000Z
- Updated: 2026-11-08T08:26:21.000Z
- Author: BigGo Editorial Team
- Keywords: Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, Meritz Securities, Hanwha Investment & Securities, Korea Investment & Securities, Hana Securities, Kim Sun-woo, Park Jun-young, Ko Young-min, KOSPI, HBM, data center regulation

## Summary

Samsung Electronics shares closed at 188,700 won (approximately $140) on the 6th, falling below the 200,000 won mark on a closing basis for the first time in about seven months. The weekly decline reached 17.60%, with foreign investors leading the selloff by net selling 2.1943 trillion won (approximately $1.6 billion) worth of shares. The trigger was concern over tighter data center regulations following the U.S. midterm elections. Brokerages assess that the 12-month forward PBR has fallen to around 1.2x, approaching historical lows. Hanwha Investment & Securities recommends buying in tranches in the 170,000–180,000 won range, while Korea Investment & Securities cites 175,000 won (approximately $130) as a strong support level. However, some caution that whether earnings forecasts are revised downward will be key to judging undervaluation.

## Content

Samsung Electronics (005930) shares have fallen below 200,000 won on a closing basis for the first time in seven months, prompting a wave of analysis from brokerages that the stock has approached valuations seen at past lows. At the same time, some cautious voices argue that it is necessary to confirm how concerns over delayed data center investment will affect actual memory demand and earnings forecasts.

According to the financial investment industry on the 8th, Samsung Electronics closed at 188,700 won (approximately $140) on the 6th, down 12,800 won (6.35%) from the previous trading day. It was the first time the closing price fell below 200,000 won since April 7 (196,500 won, approximately $140), about seven months ago. During intraday trading, the stock fell as low as 179,200 won (approximately $130), briefly breaking below the 180,000 won level. The stock, which stood at 229,000 won (approximately $170) on the 2nd, declined for four consecutive trading days, bringing the weekly drop to 17.60%. Compared with the year's highest closing price of 362,500 won (approximately $270) recorded on June 18, the stock has plunged 47.94% in half a year.

Foreign investors led the selling. Foreigners net sold 2.1943 trillion won (approximately $1.6 billion) worth of Samsung Electronics shares from the 2nd to the 6th, while individuals net bought 2.3747 trillion won (approximately $1.7 billion) worth during the same period, absorbing the supply. However, the scale of foreign net selling shrank rapidly from 1.186 trillion won (approximately $869.8 million) on the 5th to 115.1 billion won (approximately $84.4 million) on the 6th.

The sharp decline was triggered by concerns over tighter data center regulations that emerged after the U.S. midterm elections. As the Democratic Party won races for the Senate, House of Representatives, and key governorships, fears spread that regulations on power and water use and environmental burdens could be strengthened. According to Eugene Investment & Securities, the five states where Democrats reclaimed governorships account for 41.2% of the total power capacity of data centers under construction or planned in the United States. The observation is that if regulations take concrete form, Big Tech's capital expenditure plans could be revised over the next two to three years, and server and memory semiconductor supply schedules could also be delayed.

Brokerage views are largely divided into two camps. First, there is the analysis that no abnormal signs have yet been detected in actual demand indicators. Kim Sun-woo, a researcher at Meritz Securities, said that after checking the U.S. sales and marketing channels of memory companies such as Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix (000660), and Micron, "no abnormal signs of demand change are being detected at the moment," and assessed that "even if demand fluctuations occur in 2028 amid confirmed demand for 2027, there is a high possibility that other customers will absorb the entire volume." He viewed the recent stock plunge as partly an exaggerated reaction to "political language" within the essence of AI competition.

Valuation indicators also point to historically low levels. Kim Rok-ho, a researcher at Hana Securities, analyzed that "the 12-month forward PBR of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix has fallen to 1.21x and 1.23x, respectively," and that "considering that the lows before experiencing the AI cycle were 0.9x and 0.8x, respectively, the lows in the AI era are likely to have leveled up to the 1.2x range." He explained that the expansion of the share of HBM, a customized product, serves as a factor lowering earnings volatility compared with the past.

Korea Investment & Securities presented 175,000 won (approximately $130) as a strong support level for Samsung Electronics. This price applies a PBR of 1.1x to estimated 2027 book value per share (BPS), about 7.3% lower than the closing price on the 6th. Ko Young-min, a researcher at Korea Investment & Securities, analyzed that "the historical low of 1.0–1.1x is not far away, which could heighten fear, but considering recent share buyback and dividend policies and the elevated earnings momentum, it is more difficult to assume the stock will break below that level."

There are also voices recommending buying in tranches based on past cycles. Park Jun-young, a researcher at Hanwha Investment & Securities, emphasized that "if Samsung Electronics had been bought at the three past lows, maximum upside opportunities of 163%, 71%, and 651% to the peak of the subsequent upcycles existed, respectively," and that "this shows that investors who took risks in historically undervalued zones were given considerable profit opportunities." He added that applying the average low PBR of about 0.94x from the three past instances yields 163,000 won (approximately $120), and suggested that a strategy of starting to buy in tranches from the 170,000–180,000 won range, equivalent to a 1.03x PBR, is reasonable.

The market's structural concentration also amplified the magnitude of this plunge. As of the closing price on the 6th, Samsung Electronics accounted for 24.27% of KOSPI market capitalization and SK Hynix for 18.19%; including Samsung Electronics preferred shares, the three securities accounted for 45.11%. This is up 13.59 percentage points from the end of last year (31.52%), reflecting a structure in which nearly half of KOSPI market capitalization is concentrated in the top two semiconductor stocks. As a result, the correction in the two stocks dragged down the entire index.

This concentration also left a clear mark on index-tracking products. The "TIGER 200 Equal Weight" ETF posted a return of -14.92% over the past month, only about half the level of the market-cap-weighted "TIGER 200" (-28.59%). This was due to the relatively larger decline in large semiconductor stocks. Park Seung-jin, a division head at Hana Securities, said, "As doubts arise about whether the AI trend can continue, future earnings estimates cannot be trusted," and added, "Valuations may look cheap now, but there are cases where earnings estimates are revised down belatedly at some point."

The key variables for restoring foreign investor sentiment are cited as rebuilding confidence in the sustainability of AI investment and shareholder return policies. Ha Jang-kwon, a researcher at Hanwha Investment & Securities, diagnosed this selloff as "a discount on the sustainability of earnings and the willingness to return capital at South Korea's top two memory companies, not on the semiconductor industry cycle," and said, "As the discount is large, the rebound could also be strong when confidence is restored." Hanwha Investment & Securities predicted that even if Samsung Electronics' earnings growth slows, rising book value could ease the PBR burden, and that the year-end dividend yield could rise to around 3% depending on the confirmation of third-quarter dividends.

Ultimately, the key question is whether concerns over delayed data center investment lead to actual downward revisions of earnings forecasts. Since low PBR is also calculated based on future net asset estimates, the basis for judging undervaluation could waver if the outlook changes. However, some observers note that since data centers are strategic resources directly linked to national competitiveness, the possibility that regulations will actually lead to a reduction in AI investment is limited. Ko Young-min, a researcher, explained that "data centers are strategic resources connected to national competitiveness," and that "in terms of the AI hegemony competition between the United States and China, a data center moratorium would amount to tolerating China's pursuit."

What are historical stock prices?

Historical stock prices refer to a stock’s recorded prices at various past points. These prices include several key figures that help investors and analysts evaluate a stock’s performance over time: Open: Open price for the trading day. High: Highest price for the trading day. Low: Lowest price for the trading day. Close: Close price for the trading day. Additionally, historical prices often include: Volume is the number of shares traded during the day. How can I use 005930.KS stock historical prices to predict future price movements?

Trend Analysis: Examine the 005930.KS stock’s historical trends to identify patterns that might continue. Moving Averages: Use moving averages to detect potential reversal points. Statistical Methods: Use statistical tools such as regression analysis to model and forecast future prices based on past data. These techniques can provide insights but should be used with risk management practices to mitigate potential losses.

---

What impact do stock splits have on historical price data?

When a company performs a stock split, it adjusts the historical price data to reflect the new, lower trading price as if it had always been that way. This ensures consistency for anyone analyzing the stock’s past prices. The adjustment helps prevent misleading signals on charts, such as false sell signals or bearish trends that aren’t there. For instance, in a 2-for-1 stock split, the price per share is cut in half, which would otherwise appear as a dramatic drop on the chart. If someone didn’t know about the split, they might wrongly think something negative happened to the company. Most technical indicators would also react to this apparent drop by signaling to sell. A stock split, while making the shares seem more affordable and potentially more attractive to investors, doesn’t alter the company’s fundamental value.

---

Why do the 005930.KS stock historical prices show a range for periods like 30 days, 90 days, and 52 weeks?

The range provides the lowest and highest prices at which the stock has traded during the specified period. This helps investors understand the stock’s volatility and price variability within that timeframe.

---

How can I use historical price volatility to assess risk?

High price volatility historically indicates higher risk and potentially higher returns. Investors can gauge the stock’s risk level by examining the range between high and low prices over various periods.

# Asia stocks tumble as AI rout batters Japan, S. Korea

Author Ayushman Ojha

Published Nov 05, 2026, 10:12 PM

Updated Nov 06, 2026, 02:10 AM

Asia stocks tumble as AI rout batters Japan, S. Korea

285A-2.46%

Investing.com-- Asian stocks tumbled Friday, with Japan and South Korea leading a broad regional selloff, as investors dumped tech shares amid growing concerns about artificial intelligence investment after the U.S. midterm elections.

The rout followed Wall Street’s steepest single-day decline in more than a year on Thursday. The S&P 500 tumbled 4.4%, the Nasdaq Composite slumped 5.5% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 3.4%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12.3%.

U.S. stock futures traded mixed in Asian trading on Friday by 07:09 GMT, with Nasdaq 100 Futures rising.

## KOSPI drop triggers trading halt; Nikkei enters bear market

South Korea’s KOSPI ended 6% lower after plunging as much as 8.8% to 4,911.28 points -- its lowest since early February. The Korea Exchange triggered a 20-minute circuit breaker after an 8% drop, temporarily suspending stock and derivatives trading.

Samsung Electronics (KS:005930) fell 6.4%, and SK Hynix (KS:000660) slid 10.4%.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 closed 6% lower, putting the benchmark more than 20% below its June record high and bringing it into bear-market territory. Japan’s broader TOPIX index also fell nearly 6%.

Semiconductor equipment maker Advantest (TYO:6857), memory-chip producer Kioxia Holdings (TYO:285A) and SoftBank Group (TYO:9984) were among the biggest losers, extending a rout in technology stocks. The selloff followed Thursday’s declines, when Advantest plunged 15%, Lasertec dropped 14%, and Kioxia fell 13%.

In the U.S., Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) shares sank nearly 10% overnight after its smartphone chip sales missed analyst estimates, adding to pressure on semiconductor companies already facing questions over elevated valuations and the returns on massive AI infrastructure investments.

The election outcome has added another layer of uncertainty. Democrats’ gains in the midterms have raised concerns that a Democrat-controlled Congress could increase scrutiny of data-centre developments and potentially slow construction, particularly in states where candidates campaigned against large-scale projects.

## Taiwan, China shares down; oil rebounds

Elsewhere in Asia, Taiwan’s technology-heavy Taiwan Weighted index fell 4.5%. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) (TW:2330) shares slipped 4.8%.

China’s Shanghai Composite fell 1.1%, while the clue-chip Shanghai Shenzhen CSI 300 declined 1.4%. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index also fell 1.2%.

Singapore’s Straits Times Index dropped 2.8%, while Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.5%.

India’s Nifty 50 rose 0.5%.

While expectations that Democrats’ election victory could accelerate efforts to end the Iran war had initially supported risk appetite, concerns over AI investment and semiconductor earnings have since taken centre stage.

Oil prices extended gains in Asian trading Friday after sharp losses earlier this week, as investors weigh uncertainty about President Donald Trump’s next move regarding Iran after the midterms.
